title: Statistics Field Guide
audience: Both curious beginners and analysts; introductory and advanced paths
scope: 42 original problem-first articles across 22 subject collections, with an additional curated traps collection, grouped browsing, and two reading paths.

patterns.title: Define the Quantity You Want to Estimate
patterns.summary: Turn a broad question into an explicit population, outcome, time horizon, and comparison.

visual.reason: Show how changing the outcome, horizon, or post-assignment population changes the estimated contrast.

collections.problem: Preserve information about shared units and distinguish local evidence from between-group variation.

collections.title: Time, Forecasting, and Monitoring
collections.problem: Evaluate future predictions using past information and connect predictive ranges to subsequent observations.

collections.title: Time to Events and Reliability
collections.problem: Use event-free observation time, respect the follow-up process, and express what rare failures can establish.

collections.title: Causal Questions and Traps
collections.problem: Specify the causal question, make assumptions visible, and avoid adjustment or timing that creates misleading comparisons.

collections.title: Finding Credible Causal Comparisons
collections.problem: Select a comparison design from the assignment mechanism, available support, and defensible assumptions.

collections.title: Challenging Causal Conclusions
collections.problem: Probe consequential assumptions through targeted checks, sensitivity analysis, and bounds.

collections.title: False Discoveries and Reproducibility
collections.problem: Retain the search history, plan monitoring, and reserve independent information for confirmation.

collections.title: Combining Evidence Across Studies
collections.problem: Compare compatible estimates, preserve heterogeneity, and investigate evidence that may be missing.

collections.title: Decisions under Uncertainty
collections.problem: Connect evidence to actions, unequal consequences, and the value of further information.

collections.title: Communicating Statistical Results
collections.problem: Explain baselines, absolute and relative effects, uncertainty, populations, and the limits of a claim.

collections.title: Discovering Hidden Structure
collections.problem: Distinguish compression, latent constructs, and exploratory grouping, then assess the resulting representation.

collections.title: Simulation and Computational Reliability
collections.problem: Check estimators and implementations against known cases while separating numerical accuracy from model adequacy.

collections.title: Sparse Data and Rare Events
collections.problem: Respond to few events, weak local information, and unstable estimates with suitable bounds or defensible sharing.

interactive_examples.title: Base rates and positive results
interactive_examples.scope: At 1% prevalence, 90% sensitivity, and 95% specificity, 10,000 submissions yield expected counts of 90 true positives and 495 false positives: about 15.4% of flags are true positives.

interactive_examples.title: Binomial uncertainty explorer
interactive_examples.scope: For 10 observed events in 100 independent trials, the 95% Wilson interval is approximately 5.52% to 17.44%. It is not a prediction interval or a universal procedure for dependent data.

interactive_examples.title: Zero-event upper bound
interactive_examples.scope: With zero events in 100 independent, fully observed trials, the one-sided 95% exact binomial upper bound is about 2.95%, under the fixed-sample model.

interactive_examples.title: Partial pooling explorer
interactive_examples.scope: With observation SD 5, population mean 0, population SD 2, and observed mean 6, the fixed normal-means example gives a pooled mean about 0.83 at n=1 and 5.65 at n=100.

interactive_examples.title: Mean and median explorer
interactive_examples.scope: One genuine extreme value can move the mean much more than the median. The appropriate summary depends on the question; numerical influence does not prove a recording error.

interactive_examples.title: Group composition explorer
interactive_examples.scope: A succeeds more often within each fictional subgroup, but B has the higher raw aggregate because it receives more easy cases. Standardizing both to a common mix changes the comparison.

interactive_examples.title: Difference-in-differences explorer
interactive_examples.scope: A treated index changing from 40 to 55 and an untreated index changing from 20 to 28 gives (55-40)-(28-20)=7. The arithmetic alone does not establish causality.

interactive_examples.title: Factorial interaction explorer
interactive_examples.scope: Temperature changes yield by 2 units with the old recipe and 17 with the new recipe, giving an additive interaction contrast of 15 units in the fictional example.

interactive_examples.title: Multiple-testing explorer
interactive_examples.scope: With 20 independent true-null tests, each with false-positive probability 0.05, the probability of at least one false positive is 1-0.95^20, about 64.2%.

limitations: A broad first edition, not an exhaustive catalog of every estimator or specialized field.
Reading paths are curated collections; advanced notes do not create a new difficulty-filter feature.
Recommendation queries are package metadata, not a new retrieval service.
Widgets are fixed-assumption teaching examples, not general statistical analysis tools.
